title: The naming
hookLine: a name chosen, a name changed, and a man who refused to change his

cards: Rough ground. Hard, rugged ground. That's what the name Hazn means, and a man who carried it comes to the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him.
The Prophet asks his name, hears it, and offers him another: Sahl, easy, smooth ground. Hazn says no. I won't change a name my father gave me.
His grandson tells this story in Sahih al-Bukhari, and adds a quiet line of his own: that roughness stayed in the family afterward. A name, in this story, is not just a label.

teach.h: HE TAUGHT ADAM ALL THE NAMES.
teach.b: Names go back to the beginning. In surah al-Baqarah, in Pickthall's translation: "And He taught Adam all the names." In the Qur'an, the names are what Allah teaches Adam.
Then, when. Some reports have the Prophet naming a baby the day it was brought to him: Abu Musa's son Ibrahim, Umm Sulaym's son 'Abdullah, both from yesterday.
Another report, in Abu Dawud and Tirmidhi, mentions naming on the seventh day, along with other things done that day that belong to the coming lessons.

teach.h: THE FIRST DAY, OR THE SEVENTH.
teach.b: So families name on the first day, or the seventh, and both have a basis. What makes a name good?
In Sahih Muslim, the Prophet says, in paraphrase: the most beloved of your names to Allah are 'Abdullah and 'Abd al-Rahman. Servant of Allah. Servant of the Most Merciful.
A name that says whose the child is. And names can be changed.
Also in Muslim, Ibn 'Umar reports that a daughter of 'Umar was named 'Asiyah, which sounds like disobedient, and the Prophet renamed her Jamilah: beautiful. That's the background to Hazn's story.

More than once, the Prophet lifted a heavy name into a lighter one, and Hazn chose to keep his. A name is one of the earliest gifts a child is handed. Every time someone calls them, its meaning gets said out loud.

how: Muslim parents choose a name with a good meaning for a newborn, on the day of birth or on the seventh day, and names such as 'Abdullah and 'Abd al-Rahman are favored after the hadith in Sahih Muslim.

games.q: the Prophet hears that a daughter of 'Umar is named 'Asiyah, a name that sounds like disobedient. what does he do?
o: asks 'Umar to wait until she is grown.
games.why: Sahih Muslim: he renamed her Jamilah, lifting a heavy name into a lighter one.

practice: Say your own name silently, slowly, the way someone who loves you says it, and wonder who chose it: for a grandparent, a saint, a sound someone liked, a hope?
If your name were a meaning said out loud every time you're called, what would you want it to say? If you pray, you can make du'a for whoever named you.

wordCard.voice: The naming. A good name given on the first day or the seventh, beloved when it says whose the child is, and changed when the meaning is heavy. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: name. the same word opens bismillah, in the name of Allah.

carryVoice: Your line: a good name. Hazn kept his; 'Asiyah became Jamilah. Tomorrow, the seventh-day sacrifice.
